lines.trans: How long do we have to wait? I want to eat.
Denis, forgive me, I am a little late.
I am not surprised at all, let's go upstairs.
Only I came for just a short while tonight.
Yeah? Why did you even bother coming then?
Well yes, you are right, I will head back.
Wait, you are not going anywhere right now.
Denis, why are you pretending to be a tough guy?
Katya, I do not know who I should be.
Always stay the way you are.
That is the exact way I liked you.
All right, I will definitely try to be myself.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.

examples.text: Сколько нужно ждать? Я хочу есть.
examples.trans: How long do we have to wait? I want to eat.
So much gum!
How much is it?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'necessary'.

examples.trans: I need to make a call.
You need to rest.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Listen, Denis, people are waiting for the order.

examples.text: Да, сейчас, меня там ждёт Нагиев.
examples.trans: Yes, right now, Nagiyev is waiting for me there.

examples.text: Сколько нужно ждать? Я хочу есть.
examples.trans: How long do we have to wait? I want to eat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: I won a lucky ticket.
No, I am not running away.
Do you feel bad with me right now?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I wanted to lift your spirits.

examples.text: Я же просто хотел тебе помочь.
examples.trans: I just wanted to help you.
Do you want some? It is very healthy.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Today will be our first day.
Look, there is one more video clip.
I wonder where all this took place?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'стить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to forgive', forming an aspectual pair with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Денис, прости меня, я немного опоздала.
examples.trans: Denis, forgive me, I am a little late.
Excuse me, who are you?
Forgive me.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a little'.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be late', forming an aspectual pair with 'опаздывать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Денис, прости меня, я немного опоздала.
examples.trans: Denis, forgive me, I am a little late.
Sorry, I'm late.
Won't we be late?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.
He's completely alone.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, I am not running away.
Chef, come on, do not keep us in suspense.

examples.text: Герман ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: German is not to blame for anything.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'surprised', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: The guest was pleasantly surprised.

examples.text: Ты будешь приятно удивлён этим супом!
examples.trans: You will be pleasantly surprised by this soup!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Let's get out of here to the kitchen faster.

examples.text: Я совсем не удивлён, пошли наверх.
examples.trans: I am not surprised at all, let's go upstairs.
May I go?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'upstairs', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я совсем не удивлён, пошли наверх.
examples.trans: I am not surprised at all, let's go upstairs.

examples.text: Сколько нужно ждать? Я хочу есть.
examples.trans: How long do we have to wait? I want to eat.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'only'.

examples.trans: But just one spark is enough.
And we are only dating starting today.
I only need the watermelon pulp.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to arrive', forming an aspectual pair with 'приезжать'.

examples.text: Только я приехала сегодня совсем ненадолго.
examples.trans: Only I came for just a short while tonight.

examples.text: Нет, я просто приехала вас поддержать.
examples.trans: No, I just came to support you.

examples.text: Или я сейчас зря сюда приехала?
examples.trans: Or did I come here in vain right now?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.trans: Are you running away again today?
And we are only dating starting today.
Today will be our first day.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'for a short time'.

examples.text: Только я приехала сегодня совсем ненадолго.
examples.trans: Only I came for just a short while tonight.
He left for a short time.

examples.text: Спасибо, я словно ненадолго вернулся домой!
examples.trans: Thank you, I felt as if I briefly returned home!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('yes') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, Katyusha, eat up, eat.
Yes, we are taking a very big risk.

examples.text: Да ты в чёрном списке посмотри.
examples.trans: Just look at the blacklist.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Why did you make this shark?
Vitya, why are you talking like that?

examples.text: Зачем ты смеёшься над чужим горем?
examples.trans: Why are you laughing at someone else's grief?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Are you running away again today?
Do you feel bad with me right now?
I feel very good with you.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.

examples.trans: Then a bright flame flares up.
He received a suspended sentence back then.
Then they will definitely lock German up fast.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.

examples.trans: I am not allowed to drink at all right now.
Are you a real man or what?

examples.text: Да? Зачем ты тогда вообще приезжала?
examples.trans: Yeah? Why did you even bother coming then?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'езжать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'приехать'.

examples.text: Да? Зачем ты тогда вообще приезжала?
examples.trans: Yeah? Why did you even bother coming then?
Come over in the evening.
Mum arrives tomorrow.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('well') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, there is a very long story there.
Chef, come on, do not keep us in suspense.
Vitya, just accept it already.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'right', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: The right foot.
You're right.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle), to set off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'ехать'.

examples.text: Ну да, ты прав, я поеду.
examples.trans: Well yes, you are right, I will head back.

examples.text: Постой, никуда ты сейчас не поедешь.
examples.trans: Wait, you are not going anywhere right now.
We'll go home.

постоять.gloss: to stand for a while; to wait

meanings.en: to stand for a while; to wait
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'стоять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to stand for a while', forming an aspectual pair with 'стоять'.

examples.text: Постой, никуда ты сейчас не поедешь.
examples.trans: Wait, you are not going anywhere right now.
Wait, don't go!
I'll stand here for a bit.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'nowhere'.

examples.text: Постой, никуда ты сейчас не поедешь.
examples.trans: Wait, you are not going anywhere right now.

examples.text: Слушайте, да не нужно вам никуда ехать.
examples.trans: Listen, you don't need to go anywhere.
I wasn't hiding anywhere!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.trans: Do you feel bad with me right now?
We have a lot of work right now.
I will slice everything up quickly right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (root 'ображать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to portray'.

examples.text: Денис, зачем ты изображаешь крутого мужика?
examples.trans: Denis, why are you pretending to be a tough guy?

examples.text: Я изображал, будто мы с ней встречаемся.
examples.trans: I pretended as if we were dating.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'cool', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Денис, зачем ты изображаешь крутого мужика?
examples.trans: Denis, why are you pretending to be a tough guy?

examples.text: Раз ты такой крутой, познакомь нас!
examples.trans: Since you're so cool, introduce us!
He has a cool car.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'man', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Always dominate, be a real man.
Are you a real man or what?

examples.text: Денис, зачем ты изображаешь крутого мужика?
examples.trans: Denis, why are you pretending to be a tough guy?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Stop it, I know him well.

examples.text: Я знал, что это когда-нибудь вспомнят.
examples.trans: I knew that they would bring this up someday.

examples.text: Я не знаю, они у него в кабинете.
examples.trans: I do not know, he keeps them in his office.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('who') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Hey there, who do we have here?
Who is having so much fun in here today?
Are you a real man or what?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to stay', forming an aspectual pair with 'остаться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Оставайся всегда таким, какой ты есть.
examples.trans: Always stay the way you are.
It is wiser to always remain yourself.
The advance stays with us.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'always'.

examples.trans: Always dominate, be a real man.

examples.text: Оставайся всегда таким, какой ты есть.
examples.trans: Always stay the way you are.

examples.text: Но кто часто врёт, всегда проигрывает.
examples.trans: But whoever lies often always loses.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('such') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: It has the exact same title.

examples.text: Мне такие мальчики совсем не нравятся.
examples.trans: I do not like boys like that at all.
Why is my knife so hot?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Really? What pills is he taking?
What a cunning scoundrel he is!

examples.text: Оставайся всегда таким, какой ты есть.
examples.trans: Always stay the way you are.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('exactly') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Именно таким ты мне и понравился.
examples.trans: That is the exact way I liked you.
Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And in the end she agreed.
He is a psychopath and very aggressive.

examples.text: И все деньги у него украли.
examples.trans: And they stole all his money from him.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'нравиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be liked', forming an aspectual pair with 'нравиться'.

examples.text: Мне кажется, вы ей очень понравились.
examples.trans: It seems to me that she liked you two a lot.

examples.text: Именно таким ты мне и понравился.
examples.trans: That is the exact way I liked you.

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.

examples.trans: I feel very good with you.
Stop it, I know him well.

examples.text: Феде сейчас так хорошо от таблеток.
examples.trans: Fedya feels so good from the pills right now.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.trans: All right, I will definitely try today.

examples.text: Хорошо, я обязательно попробую быть собой.
examples.trans: All right, I will definitely try to be myself.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.

examples.trans: All right, I will definitely try today.

examples.text: Ну что, может, мы уже попробуем?
examples.trans: Well then, maybe we will taste it already?

examples.text: Хорошо, я обязательно попробую быть собой.
examples.trans: All right, I will definitely try to be myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Его так легко вывести из себя?
examples.trans: Is it that easy to make him lose his temper?
You have warmed a snake on your chest.
Stop behaving like a pushover.
